method: Reviewed official publisher and UPLB repository text and reuse policies. On 2026-11-01, the full JESAM and PJS PDFs were readable in their official web-text views although prior direct fetches returned HTTP 403. Both screenshot endpoints returned cache misses, so no table cell or species-by-site matrix was visually verified or transcribed; no local copies were retained.

surveys.sourceReports: The official full-text web view reports 16 source-classified taxa, 13 genera, 10 families and 4,920 individuals from three Makiling Forest Reserve sites; site richness is 12 at Dampalit Falls, 12 at Molawin Creek and 9 at Cambantoc River. One results sentence incorrectly calls 4,920 'species'; Table 1 includes a genus-level Rhinogobius sp. entry.
surveys.dateLimit: The paper's received date is 2010-04-29; no collection date was established from the accessible primary indexed text.
surveys.waterbodyScope: The names match existing Makiling research leads, but this batch does not change their scope assignments.
surveys.taxonomy: The paper cites FishBase 2010 and Catalogue of Fishes 2011. Current accepted names/statuses were not crosschecked; Rhinogobius sp. is genus-level, and spellings including Poecilia latippina and Xiphophorus helleri remain source strings.
surveys.reuse: PJS describes the journal as open access, while its author guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form. No article-level open reuse license was found. No table or taxa rows are redistributed in this review.
surveys.access: Official PJS full text was read in its web-text view on 2026-11-01; earlier direct article/PDF requests returned HTTP 403, and the PDF screenshot endpoint returned cache miss. No local copy or visual table review.

surveys.sourceReports: The full-text web view reports 1,474 individuals and 15 taxa for the selected diminutive-fish survey across a multi-area river system. Representative specimens were sent to the UPLB Museum of Natural History for verification; no accession numbers are supplied in the text reviewed.
surveys.waterbodyScope: The source describes Nagcarlan and Liliw upstream, Magdalena midstream, and Sta. Cruz downstream, while Table 1 labels the four sites Nagcarlan, Liliw, Calumpang, and Sta. Cruz. The Magdalena/Calumpang difference and correspondence to the single Sta Cruz River scope lead remain unresolved; no assignment or alias was added.
surveys.taxonomy: The table's searchable text is column-disordered and could not be visually verified. Source strings including Glossogobius cf. illimis and Micropis brachyurus brachyurus, plus the paper's first-Philippine-record statement for Dawkinsia arulius, require source/specimen and current-authority review; no name was normalized.
surveys.reuse: The UKDR policy says authors assign article copyright to UKDR, subject to enumerated personal-use exceptions. No open reuse license for this article was identified. No table or taxa rows are redistributed in this review.
surveys.access: Official UPLB JESAM full text was read in its web-text view on 2026-11-01; direct PDF open returned HTTP 403 and PDF screenshot returned cache miss. No local copy or visual table review.

rightsPolicySources.title: About PJS
rightsPolicySources.finding: The journal calls itself open access; this page did not establish an item-level reuse license for the 2011 article.

rightsPolicySources.title: PJS Author's Guide
rightsPolicySources.finding: The author guide states that authors sign a copyright-transfer form when a manuscript is accepted.

rightsPolicySources.title: JESAM policies
rightsPolicySources.finding: The policies state that authors assign article copyright to UKDR, with defined personal-use exceptions; they do not grant a third-party public data-reuse license.

limitations: The Santa Cruz table extraction is not visually verified and is not suitable for transcribing fine-grained station cells.
The Paller survey's collection date is unresolved; its 2010 received date and 2011 publication date are not collection dates.
The Santa Cruz River System's sites may not be equivalent to the scope registry's single Sta Cruz River lead; the methods' Magdalena label conflicts with the table's Calumpang label.
The Santa Cruz result is restricted to diminutive fishes below the authors' 100 mm standard-adult-length threshold, rather than all fish in the river system.
The Paller paper's full text reports no field dates, and its source table was not visually checked. Its hook-and-line earthworm method is not diet evidence or a general bait recommendation.
Neither study establishes present-day species presence, abundance, catchability, natural diet, safety or fishing legality.
nextAction: Request an author or UPLB Museum of Natural History station crosswalk and specimen accession details. If species-level reuse is needed, obtain written permission, visually inspect the table, reconcile source identifications with current taxonomy, and keep the historical size-selected survey separate from present-day evidence. Continue independently reusable CALABARZON freshwater research in parallel.
